findings.title: Store::create panics with unwrap on None when updating quota for a new owner
findings.description: self.quota starts empty in Store::new() and no code ever inserts initial entries. Calling self.quota.get_mut(owner).unwrap() returns None and panics on the first link created for any owner, crashing the worker thread and poisoning the store mutex.

findings.title: Store::resolve has an inverted expiration comparison that deletes valid links
findings.description: The expiration check computes `SystemTime::now() < link.expires_at`, which evaluates to true while the link is still valid. As a result, resolving any active link immediately deletes it from the store and returns None, whereas already-expired links are resolved and kept.

findings.title: Store::page sets slice end to all.len() + 1 and panics out of bounds
findings.description: When `offset + size > all.len()`, `end` is clamped to `all.len() + 1` instead of `all.len()`. Slicing `all[offset..end]` on line 92 then panics with an out-of-bounds index whenever a requested page extends past the number of stored links (including default calls from `/links` and `/report`).

findings.title: bearer_token panics on empty or single-token Authorization header
findings.description: `bearer_token` splits `header` on `' '` and unconditionally indexes `parts[1]`. When a request omits the `Authorization` header (passing `""`) or sends a header value without a space, `parts` has length 1 and `parts[1]` panics with an index-out-of-bounds error.

findings.title: Authenticator::require_admin uses || instead of && and rejects every session
findings.description: The condition `if session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner"` is always true because a single string cannot equal both `"admin"` and `"owner"` at the same time. Consequently, `require_admin` unconditionally returns `Err("admin role required")` even for admin and owner sessions.

findings.title: Authenticator::verify never checks session.expires_at
findings.description: `Session` carries an `expires_at` timestamp and `verify` is documented to return an error when a token's lifetime has run out, but `verify` returns `Ok(session.clone())` as soon as `session.token == token` without checking whether `SystemTime::now() >= session.expires_at`.

findings.title: Server::stats divides by zero when the store is empty
findings.description: In `stats`, `let per_link = hits / guard.len() as i64;` divides by `guard.len()` without checking if the store is empty. Calling `GET /stats` when no links exist panics with division by zero and poisons the store mutex.

findings.title: Server::handle calls read_to_end on the TCP stream, hanging standard HTTP clients
findings.description: `stream.read_to_end(&mut body)` blocks until the client closes its write side of the TCP connection (EOF). Standard HTTP/1.1 clients keep the connection open while awaiting the response, causing requests to hang indefinitely.

findings.title: Server::redirect lowercases the link code before resolving
findings.description: `redirect` calls `guard.resolve(&code.to_lowercase())`, but `validate_code` allows uppercase ASCII letters (`is_ascii_alphanumeric()`). Any link imported or renamed with uppercase letters in its code can never be resolved through `/l`.

findings.title: write_snapshot ignores fs::rename errors and renames across /tmp and dir
findings.description: `write_snapshot` creates its temporary file in `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json`, does not flush/sync it to disk, and discards the result of `fs::rename(&tmp, Path::new(dir).join("snapshot.json"))` with `let _ =`. When `/tmp` and `dir` reside on different filesystems, `fs::rename` fails with `EXDEV`, and any rename failure is silently swallowed while returning `Ok(())`.

findings.title: archive_all silently ignores file write errors
findings.description: Inside `archive_all`, `let _ = write!(file, ...)` discards any I/O error while writing link records, allowing truncated or empty CSV files to be produced while returning `Ok(())`.

findings.title: read_report does not default an empty report name to "links" like export_csv
findings.description: When `name` is empty, `export_csv` defaults `name` to `"links"` and writes `links.csv`, but `read_report` uses `name` verbatim and tries to read `.csv`. Calling `GET /report` without `?name=` therefore writes `links.csv` and then fails with HTTP 500 when reading it back.

findings.title: Cache::set evicts an arbitrary HashMap key instead of the least recently used entry
findings.description: `Cache::set` is documented to evict the least recently used entry and `Cache::get` maintains `entry.used = Instant::now()`, but `set` picks `guard.keys().next().cloned()`, which evicts an arbitrary key in hash-table order instead of the entry with the oldest `used` timestamp (and also evicts an entry even when updating an existing key at capacity).

findings.title: Cache::utilization truncates to 0 due to integer division and panics if limit is 0
findings.description: `guard.len() / self.limit * 100` performs integer division before multiplying by 100, which evaluates to 0 whenever `guard.len() < self.limit` (0%–99% full), and panics with division by zero if `self.limit == 0`.

findings.title: Cache::peek reports expired entries as present
findings.description: `Cache::peek` checks `guard.contains_key(code)` without checking whether `Instant::now() > entry.expires`. Expired entries still in the map cause `peek` to return `true` and prevent `Cache::warm` from refreshing them.

findings.title: load_config sets timeout to 0ms on invalid LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS instead of keeping default
findings.description: When `LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS` fails to parse as `u64`, `load_config` prints `"keeping default"` but then assigns `cfg.timeout = Duration::from_millis(0)`, overwriting the 10-second default with a zero timeout.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS is converted with Duration::from_secs instead of Duration::from_millis
findings.description: `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` is documented and named as a duration in milliseconds, but `load_config` constructs `Duration::from_secs(n)`, making the cache TTL 1,000 times longer than configured.

findings.title: load_config discards parsed LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT instead of setting cfg.fetch_limit
findings.description: After parsing `LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT` and checking `if limit > 0`, `load_config` executes `let _ = limit;` and never assigns `cfg.fetch_limit = limit;`.

findings.title: Config::validate always returns Ok(()) even when validation problems are found
findings.description: `Config::validate` collects errors into `problems` and prints them, but always returns `Ok(())` at line 113 instead of `Err(...)`, so `cfg.validate().unwrap()` never rejects invalid configurations at startup.

findings.title: Store::rename validates `from` twice and never validates `to`
findings.description: `Store::rename` calls `validate_code(from)?` twice on lines 70–71 and never calls `validate_code(to)?`, allowing a link to be renamed to an invalid target code.

findings.title: Store::success_rate always returns 0 for partial hit rates due to integer division
findings.description: `(used / self.links.len() * 100) as u32` divides two `usize` values before multiplying by 100. Whenever `used < self.links.len()`, `used / self.links.len()` truncates to 0, so any success rate below 100% is reported as 0%.

findings.title: Store::delete does not decrement the owner's quota count
findings.description: `Store::delete` is documented to return the owner's quota slot when a link is removed, but it discards `link.owner` with `let _ = link.owner;` and leaves `self.quota` unchanged.

findings.title: Store::top sorts ascending by hits and returns the least followed links
findings.description: `Store::top` is documented to return the `n` most followed links with most hits first, but `all.sort_by(|a, b| a.hits.cmp(&b.hits))` sorts in ascending order before truncating, returning the `n` links with the fewest hits.

findings.title: Store::by_owner matches owners by substring instead of exact equality
findings.description: `by_owner` filters links with `l.owner.contains(owner)` instead of `l.owner == owner`, returning links owned by any user whose identifier contains `owner` as a substring.

findings.title: Store::extend revives expired links and overwrites expires_at from now instead of extending it
findings.description: `Store::extend` is documented to push a link's expiry out by `ttl` while keeping already-expired links expired. Instead, it does not check whether the link has already expired and sets `link.expires_at = SystemTime::now() + ttl`, reviving dead links and shortening the lifetime of links whose remaining TTL exceeds `ttl`.

findings.title: Store::quotas returns a mutable reference to internal state instead of a snapshot
findings.description: `Store::quotas` is documented as returning a snapshot whose mutation must not affect the store, but its signature `pub fn quotas(&mut self) -> &mut HashMap<String, u32>` directly exposes the internal `self.quota` map to mutation.

findings.title: Store::import is not atomic and partially mutates the store on validation failure
findings.description: `Store::import` is documented to insert either every link in the batch or none of them, leaving the store untouched on error. Because it inserts each link inside the same loop that calls `validate_code(&link.code)?`, any invalid code after the first element leaves earlier links inserted in `self.links`.

findings.title: Store::prune returns the number of remaining links instead of the number removed
findings.description: `Store::prune` is documented to report how many links it removed and saves `let before = self.links.len();`, but then ignores `before` and returns `self.links.len()` (the count of remaining links).

findings.title: start_janitor leaks the background thread when JanitorStop is dropped
findings.description: `start_janitor` documents that the returned `JanitorStop` handle stops the sweep when dropped, but `rx.try_recv().is_ok()` only exits on an explicit `send(())` and ignores `Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected)` when `JanitorStop` is dropped.

findings.title: Self-deadlock in count_by_owner from locking non-reentrant Mutex twice
findings.description: count_by_owner acquires store.lock().unwrap() on line 120 (`guard`) and then calls store.lock().unwrap() again on line 122 (`second`) while `guard` is still in scope. Because std::sync::Mutex is not reentrant, any thread calling count_by_owner blocks forever waiting on the lock it already holds, permanently wedging the calling thread and every other thread that accesses `store`.

findings.title: ABBA lock-ordering deadlock between Cache::get and Cache::flush
findings.description: Cache::get acquires `self.entries.write()` (line 33) and, while holding it, acquires `self.hits.lock()` (line 45). Cache::flush acquires `self.hits.lock()` (line 116) first and then acquires `self.entries.write()` (line 117). If Thread A is in `get` holding `entries` and waiting for `hits` while Thread B is in `flush` holding `hits` and waiting for `entries`, both threads deadlock permanently and block all subsequent cache accesses.

findings.title: Lost updates in Metrics::add_resolved due to non-atomic load-then-store
findings.description: Metrics::add_resolved performs a separate `self.resolved.load(Ordering::Relaxed)` followed by `self.resolved.store(current + 1, Ordering::Relaxed)`. When two request handler threads concurrently resolve links via `/l` or `/out`, both threads can load the same `current` value before either stores `current + 1`, losing increments.

findings.title: warm_cache detaches spawned threads instead of joining them before returning
findings.description: warm_cache spawns a thread for each `(code, target)` pair and pushes the `JoinHandle`s into `handles`, but then drops the vector with `let _ = handles;` on line 90 without calling `.join()`. Dropping `JoinHandle` detaches the threads rather than waiting for them, so `warm_cache` returns before the cache is populated and races with subsequent callers.

findings.title: Janitor thread leaks when JanitorStop is dropped and blocks shutdown during sleep
findings.description: start_janitor documents that dropping `JanitorStop` stops the sweep, but line 54 only exits on `if rx.try_recv().is_ok()`. When `JanitorStop` is dropped without calling `stop()`, `tx` is dropped and `rx.try_recv()` returns `Err(TryRecvError::Disconnected)`, for which `.is_ok()` is false, leaking the background thread forever. Additionally, sleeping with `thread::sleep(interval)` ignores stop signals for up to `interval` and runs another sweep before re-checking, and line 59 holds the `store` mutex across `cache.sweep()` on line 65.

findings.title: check_targets uses zero-capacity channel and retains sender in receiver thread
findings.description: check_targets creates an unbuffered `mpsc::sync_channel(0)` and keeps the original `tx` alive in the parent scope while looping `for _ in 0..targets.len()` on `rx.recv()`. Every worker thread blocks on `tx.send(outcome)` waiting for the main thread, and if any worker thread panics or exits without sending, `rx.recv()` on line 109 deadlocks forever because the parent thread still holds its own `tx` handle so the channel never disconnects.

findings.title: TOCTOU race in Cache::sweep can delete freshly updated cache entries
findings.description: Cache::sweep collects expired keys while holding a read lock on `self.entries`, drops the read lock on line 103, and then calls `self.delete(&code)` for each key on line 105. If another thread calls `cache.set(&code, new_target)` between `drop(guard)` and `self.delete(&code)`, `sweep` unconditionally removes the newly written, non-expired entry.

findings.title: TOCTOU race in Cache::warm between peek and set
findings.description: Cache::warm checks `!self.peek(code)` under a read lock (line 86) and then calls `self.set(code, target)` under a separate write lock (line 87). If another thread inserts or updates `code` (or fills the cache to `self.limit`) between `peek` and `set`, `warm` overwrites the newer entry and can evict an existing entry in `set` even though `code` is already present.

findings.title: Missing socket timeouts and unbounded thread spawning leak handler threads
findings.description: main spawns an unbounded thread per TCP connection (line 55) and `Server::handle` calls `stream.read_to_end(&mut body)` (line 66) without configuring `self.cfg.timeout` on the socket or bounding concurrency with `self.cfg.fetch_limit`. Any client that keeps the connection open without sending EOF (such as standard HTTP/1.1 persistent connections or slow clients) blocks `read_to_end` indefinitely and leaks the handler thread.

findings.title: Global store Mutex is held across disk and network I/O in request handlers
findings.description: In `Server::report` (line 215) as well as `create_link`, `redirect`, `list_links`, `delete_link`, `admin_quotas`, and `stats`, the `self.store.lock().unwrap()` guard is kept alive while writing CSV files to disk and writing HTTP responses to `TcpStream`. A slow disk operation or stalled client holds the global `store` mutex for the duration of the I/O, blocking all other request threads and the janitor thread.

findings.title: Concurrent write_snapshot calls race on fixed temporary file path
findings.description: write_snapshot always writes to the hardcoded path `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json` (line 46) before renaming it to `snapshot.json`. If two threads invoke `write_snapshot` concurrently, their `File::create` and `write_all` calls interleave on the same temporary file and one thread's `fs::rename` removes the file out from under the other, corrupting the snapshot.

findings.title: Session tokens are generated with a timestamp-seeded LCG instead of a CSPRNG
findings.description: Authenticator::issue mints session tokens using a deterministic linear congruential generator seeded solely with SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().as_secs(). Because the seed has one-second resolution, an attacker who knows or guesses the approximate second a session was created can compute the exact bearer token offline and hijack the user or admin session.

findings.title: Admin authorization check trusts client-supplied X-Admin request header
findings.description: Server::admin_quotas authorizes access to /admin/quotas by checking whether the client sent the HTTP header X-Admin: true instead of checking the authenticated session's role. Any regular authenticated user can escalate privileges and access admin endpoints simply by adding X-Admin: true to their request.

findings.title: Path traversal in export_csv and read_report allows arbitrary .csv file write and read
findings.description: export_csv (line 13) and read_report (line 67) pass the user-controlled ?name= query parameter directly to Path::new(dir).join(format!("{}.csv", name)), and archive_all (line 33) does the same with owner. In Rust, joining a path containing '../' traverses outside dir, and joining an absolute path replaces dir entirely, allowing an authenticated attacker calling GET /report?name=... to overwrite or read arbitrary .csv files on the filesystem.

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback secret used when LINKD_SECRET is unset
findings.description: Authenticator::new silently falls back to the hardcoded constant "dev-secret-do-not-use" when the LINKD_SECRET environment variable is not set. Any deployment that omits LINKD_SECRET operates with a publicly known secret value.

findings.title: Plaintext bearer session tokens are written to stdout logs
findings.description: Authenticator::issue logs every newly minted bearer token in plaintext via println!("auth: issued token {} for {}", session.token, owner). Anyone with access to application logs or log aggregation pipelines can steal active session tokens and impersonate users.

findings.title: Authenticator::verify never checks session expiration and uses non-constant-time comparison
findings.description: Although Session tracks an expires_at timestamp and verify is documented to reject expired tokens, verify only checks session.token == token without verifying SystemTime::now() < session.expires_at. Issued tokens remain valid indefinitely unless explicitly revoked, and comparing tokens with == leaks token bytes via timing.

findings.title: Broken role condition in require_admin rejects all sessions
findings.description: Authenticator::require_admin checks if session.role != "admin" || session.role != "owner". Because a single role string cannot equal both "admin" and "owner" at the same time, the condition is always true and rejects all callers, including legitimate administrators.

findings.title: hash_password uses an unsalted 64-bit DJB2 non-cryptographic checksum
findings.description: hash_password computes a 64-bit DJB2a checksum with no salt and no work factor. An attacker who obtains stored password hashes can invert or find collisions for the 64-bit non-cryptographic checksum in milliseconds to compromise user accounts.

findings.title: bearer_token panics on missing or malformed Authorization headers
findings.description: bearer_token splits the Authorization header on ' ' and unconditionally indexes parts[1]. Any request without an Authorization header or without a space in the header value triggers an out-of-bounds panic in the handler thread before verify can return 401.

findings.title: create_link accepts the link owner from the untrusted request payload instead of the authenticated session
findings.description: Server::handle verifies the caller's token into a Session but discards it, and create_link reads owner from the POST body (fields.get("owner")). Any authenticated user can spoof another user's owner identifier to create links in their name or exhaust their quota.

findings.title: delete_link allows any authenticated user to delete any other user's link
findings.description: Despite the doc comment stating that a link may only be deleted by the user who created it using the owner from the authenticated session, delete_link calls guard.delete(&code) without checking link ownership. Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary links belonging to other owners.

findings.title: Open redirect in GET /out via unvalidated next query parameter
findings.description: Server::out takes the ?next= query parameter and issues a 301 redirect to that value without validating the scheme or host. Attackers can craft links to /out?next=https://attacker.example in emails to redirect users to phishing or malicious sites.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS origin combined with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on all responses
findings.description: Server::respond sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true on every HTTP response. Allowing wildcard cross-origin access on authenticated endpoints enables arbitrary third-party websites to read sensitive responses from the API.

findings.title: CRLF injection / HTTP response splitting in redirect_to Location header
Insecure predictable /tmp filename in write_snapshot enables symlink and TOCTOU attacks
findings.description: write_snapshot writes to a fixed path /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json in the world-writable /tmp directory using File::create. A local attacker can place a symlink at /tmp/linkd-snapshot.json to overwrite arbitrary files owned by the service user, or race between write_all and fs::rename to tamper with or read the snapshot.

findings.title: Store::by_owner uses substring matching instead of exact equality, leaking other users' links
findings.description: Store::by_owner filters links with l.owner.contains(owner) rather than l.owner == owner. A caller querying with a short owner name (such as "a") or an empty string receives links belonging to every other user whose owner identifier contains that substring.

findings.title: new_code generates predictable short link codes from subsec_nanos
findings.description: new_code derives short codes purely from SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap().subsec_nanos() formatted as hex (< 30 bits of entropy). An attacker can easily guess or brute-force private link codes created around a known time, and hash collisions in Store::create silently overwrite existing links.

findings.title: secret_eq returns early on the first mismatched byte, enabling timing attacks
findings.description: secret_eq is documented as a constant-time comparison to prevent byte-by-byte timing recovery, but the loop immediately returns false on the first mismatched byte (if x != y { return false; }). Attackers can measure response time differences to infer secret tokens one byte at a time.

findings.title: Unescaped target URL in create_link response enables JSON injection
findings.description: create_link builds a JSON response via format!("{{\"code\":\"{}\",\"target\":\"{}\"}}", link.code, link.target) without escaping double quotes or backslashes in link.target. A target URL containing '"' breaks out of the JSON string value and injects arbitrary JSON properties into the response.

findings.title: Unescaped fields in export_csv and archive_all allow CSV and formula injection
findings.description: export_csv (line 18) and archive_all (line 36) write link.target and link.owner into CSV rows without escaping commas, quotes, newlines, or spreadsheet formula prefixes ('=', '+', '-', '@'). An attacker can inject arbitrary rows into exported reports or trigger formula execution when an admin opens the CSV in a spreadsheet client.

findings.title: export_csv creates sensitive multi-owner report files with default world-readable permissions
findings.description: Although export_csv states that the report contains every owner's links and must only be readable by the service user, fs::write(&path, body) creates the file with the process's default umask (typically 0644), allowing other local users on the host to read the exported CSV.

findings.title: Store::rename validates from twice and never validates the destination code to
findings.description: Store::rename calls validate_code(from)? twice on lines 70-71 and never calls validate_code(to)?. A caller can rename a link to an unvalidated code containing invalid characters, path traversal sequences, or lengths exceeding MAX_CODE_LEN.

findings.title: 401 response reflects the caller's raw bearer token in the response body
findings.description: When authentication fails, Server::handle responds with format!("unauthorized: unknown token (token {})", token), echoing the raw token back in the HTTP response body where it may be recorded in proxy logs or exposed to cross-origin readers.

findings.title: Error responses in report leak internal server filesystem paths and OS errors
findings.description: When export_csv or read_report fails in Server::report (lines 223 and 229), the server sends the internal export directory path and raw OS error string in the 500 HTTP response body, disclosing filesystem layout to clients.
